record.original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field K, and let D1 be an admissible subcategory of Db(X1) and D2 an admissible subcategory of Db(X2). Must every exact fully faithful functor F: D1 -> D2 be of Fourier-Mukai type?

evidence.quote: Question 1.7. Is any exact fully faithful functor F : D1 -> D2 between admissible subcategories Di -> Db (Xi ), for Xi smooth projective over K, of Fourier-Mukai type?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and let $X_1, X_2$ be smooth projective varieties over $K$. Denote by $D^b(X_i)$ the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X_i$. Recall that a full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal{D} \subset D^b(X)$ is called admissible if the inclusion functor admits both a left and a right adjoint. An exact functor $F\colon \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ between triangulated subcategories $\mathcal{D}_i \subset D^b(X_i)$ is said to be of Fourier–Mukai type if there exists an object $E \in D^b(X_1 \times_K X_2)$ such that $F$ is isomorphic to the restriction to $\mathcal{D}_1$ of the functor
$$\Phi_E(-) := R(p_2)_*\bigl(E \otimes^L p_1^*(-)\bigr)\colon D^b(X_1) \to D^b(X_2),$$
where $p_1, p_2$ denote the two projections from $X_1 \times_K X_2$.

Question: Let $\mathcal{D}_1 \subset D^b(X_1)$ and $\mathcal{D}_2 \subset D^b(X_2)$ be admissible subcategories. Must every exact fully faithful functor $F\colon \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ be of Fourier–Mukai type?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every exact fully faithful functor between admissible subcategories of bounded derived categories of smooth projective varieties is of Fourier–Mukai type generalizes Orlov's representability theorem. Surveys and recent work by Canonaco–Stellari describe this as an open problem; Orlov's theorem covers the case where the source is the full $D^b(X_1)$, but the admissible-subcategory version is not known in general.

status_evidence.title: Fourier–Mukai functors: a survey (Canonaco–Stellari)
status_evidence.snippet: problems are widely open but any improvement ... may give new important impulses to the theory
status_evidence.claim: Open problems on Fourier–Mukai representability beyond Orlov's setting remain open.

status_evidence.title: An example of a non-Fourier-Mukai functor (Rizzardo–Van den Bergh)
status_evidence.snippet: non-Fourier-Mukai functor between derived categories of coherent sheaves
status_evidence.claim: Without fully faithful hypothesis there exist non-Fourier-Mukai functors; the fully faithful admissible case is not settled.
